description: Keep your async EWS Managed API code (Microsoft.Exchange.WebServices.NETStandard) and run it on Microsoft Graph. Commercial license. Not affiliated with Microsoft.
releaseNotes: Calendars an application created through EWS or MAPI, which Microsoft Graph's calendar list leaves out, work like any other calendar: with the optional MailboxFolder.Read.All permission they appear in folder listings and FindItem, CalendarView, GetItem, SyncFolderItems and notifications read them; renaming, moving, copying and deleting them, and creating a calendar inside a folder other than Calendar, need MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All. MoveFolder and CopyFolder work for calendars, with their items and subfolders; a moved calendar and its items get new IDs. With MailboxFolder.Read.All, FindFolder and SyncFolderHierarchy list folders of every kind under any folder, also under mail folders, Deleted Items and Contacts, as EWS does. Notifications: a deleted item arrives as a move to Recoverable Items, as in Exchange (for calendar items, contacts and tasks with the optional MailboxItem.Read.All permission), and so do the items of a deleted folder and an item recovered from Recoverable Items; a folder whose items changed gets a ModifiedEvent with the UnreadCount Exchange gives; a subscription to all folders also covers calendars outside the Calendar folder; subscriptions made one after another start from the same watermark. User configuration objects of every name, in any folder, with dictionary, XML and binary data, through Microsoft Graph's userConfiguration API, which is in preview (optional MailboxConfigItem.ReadWrite permission); without it CategoryList and WorkHours work as before. With the same permission GetUserRetentionPolicyTags returns the mailbox's retention policy tags, and a message gets its RetentionDate as soon as it is tagged. MarkAsJunk puts the sender on the blocked senders list or takes them off, also with MoveItem=false. FindPeople makes one persona of the contacts Exchange links as one person, also across contact folders, with Exchange's persona ID; the query searches the contact fields Exchange searches, and search results are sorted by display name. GetUserPhoto returns the stored photo whatever size is requested, as Exchange Online does. IconIndex names the SMS icons. A new post no longer shows up for a moment as a message in its folder. The license check no longer compares the key's update date with the package's release date. The README lists Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All, which Microsoft Graph requires from 31 December 2026 to change the subject, body, recipients or extended properties of received and sent messages. Security: the types in Sunsetless.Ews.Core.dll are internal apart from SunsetlessEwsOptions, so the library runs only through ExchangeService. SUNSETLESS_DENY_CROSS_MAILBOX_ACCESS also covers out-of-office settings, inbox rules named by a mailbox address and SetUserPhoto, and without impersonation it takes the request's own mailbox from X-AnchorMailbox or SUNSETLESS_DEFAULT_MAILBOX. EWS traces with HTTP headers show the Authorization header redacted. Characters that XML does not allow are removed from responses instead of failing them. A redirect from Microsoft Graph never carries the token to another host, and a request with a body does not leave Graph. A POST is not retried after 504, or after 503 without Retry-After, so a message cannot go out twice. The token is requested for the host in GraphBaseUri. A certificate read from a file keeps its key in memory only on Windows. Cookies are not shared between tenants, the Autodiscover and per-mailbox caches have an upper bound, and XML parsing refuses DTDs.
